title: Shifted and Threshold Matroids: the three-block threshold case of the main theorem (Lemma 5.1)
author: Ethan Partida
difficulty_reason: Supplying the paper's own prerequisites - the circuit classification of shifted matroids (source label lem:circuits), the component-wise partial order, the sorted concatenation operation and its monotonicity (source labels lem:weaker_prec, lem:prec_conc), the reduction of thresholdness to 2-uniform asummability (source labels lem:robust_leq, def:trade_robust, lem:thresh_contract) and the main-theorem case split (Theorem C) - still leaves a source-local argument that is not a qualifying-examination exercise. The counted proof has to produce, from nothing but the block data lambda_1, lambda_3 and the endpoints t_1, t_2, t_3, a cubic weight function w whose three finite branches are chosen so that w is weakly decreasing; it must verify the two monotonicity identities by exact polynomial algebra, compute w(T) = lambda_1 > 0, then use the circuit classification to enumerate the two families C and D of non-loop circuits of size less than the rank, and finally dominate the weight of every size-k non-basis that contains such a circuit by two further polynomial computations that are strictly negative. Every step is carried by the paper's own circuit analysis and by explicit polynomial identities rather than by quoting a textbook, which places the unit beyond ordinary PhD qualification problems in combinatorics.
